evals.name: same-facts-four-media
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. A paid event called Deck First Read happens on 17 September 2026 at 17:00 IST at Method, Bandra West, Mumbai. The fee is ₹12,000, due 10 September; bank details are on page one of the invoice. The venue has step-free entry. Guests RSVP by replying to hello@example.com. Public registration is at example.com/first-read. The client must decide by 8 September whether the session may be recorded. Write four artifacts: (1) a client email asking for the recording decision, (2) an invoice note, (3) a guest invitation, and (4) a website announcement.
evals.expected_output: Four ready-to-use artifacts with family resemblance but different structures and registers. Each artifact selects the facts its medium needs. The client decision is immediately visible; payment details are exact; invitation logistics are complete; website copy explains the offer and registration action.
assertions: The client email asks for a recording decision by 8 September 2026
The invoice note includes ₹12,000, 10 September 2026, and page-one bank details
The invitation includes date, time, venue, step-free entry, and the RSVP email
The website announcement includes the public registration URL
The four artifacts are visibly different in structure rather than four variants of one template

evals.name: constrained-style
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Make this very Apple: exactly eight short, clever two-beat lines, lots of full stops. Return only those eight lines, including the CTA. Service facts: we give founders a first-read review of an existing pitch deck, return one annotated PDF and a 45-minute call within five working days, charge ₹18,000, and never redesign the deck. Write the landing-page opening and CTA.
evals.expected_output: Exactly eight two-beat lines carry a useful proposition, deliverables, boundary, price, turnaround, and concrete CTA. The requested form is preserved without borrowed slogans, invented proof, or an unsolicited alternative.
assertions: The entire output is exactly eight nonblank lines, including the CTA, with no preface or afterword
Each line has two short beats separated by a full stop
The output states that the service reviews an existing pitch deck
The output states the annotated PDF, 45-minute call, five-working-day turnaround, ₹18,000 fee, and no-redesign boundary
The CTA names a concrete action or destination
The output uses original, meaningful lines rather than borrowed slogans or invented service claims

evals.name: invoice-clarity
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing in Write mode. Draft a payment reminder to Arun for invoice PD-104, final deck handover, ₹84,000, due 4 August 2026, now unpaid. Payment details are on page one. Ask him to reply if payment has already been sent or anything is wrong.
evals.expected_output: Calm, exact, dignified reminder. Amount, invoice, reason, due date, status, payment route, and reply action are unmistakable. No money joke or apologetic billing language.
assertions: The reminder includes invoice PD-104, ₹84,000, and 4 August 2026
The reminder identifies final deck handover as the reason
The reminder points to payment details on page one
The reminder asks for a reply if paid or if something is wrong
The reminder contains no joke about money and no apology for charging

evals.name: invitation-completeness
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Write a warm wedding invitation for Nila and Tara. Ceremony: 21 November 2026 at 16:30. Venue: The Courtyard, 14 Lake Road, Kolkata. Dinner and dancing follow. RSVP to tara@example.com by 1 October. The venue is wheelchair accessible. Children are welcome. Dress: whatever makes you feel magnificent.
evals.expected_output: Alive and welcoming invitation with personality belonging to the people and occasion. All logistics remain literal and easy to scan.
assertions: The invitation includes both names, 21 November 2026, and 16:30
The invitation includes the full venue name and address
The invitation includes the RSVP email and 1 October deadline
The invitation states wheelchair access, that children are welcome, and the dress guidance
Any humour or poetry does not obscure logistics

evals.name: apology-accountability
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing in Sensitive mode. Rewrite this: ‘Sorry the deck was late. We had a chaotic week and the client sent changes at the last minute, so there wasn't much we could do. Anyway, hope it didn't cause too much trouble. We're committed to doing better!’ Facts: we missed Friday's deadline; Priya had to present from an old file on Monday; the corrected deck is attached; we added a Thursday preflight check owned by Em.
evals.expected_output: Responsibility, concrete impact, apology, attached repair, and preventive change. No blame transfer, minimisation, wit, or request for reassurance.
assertions: The apology states that the writer missed Friday's deadline
The apology states that Priya had to present from an old file on Monday
The apology says the corrected deck is attached
The apology names the Thursday preflight check and Em's ownership
The apology does not blame the client or the chaotic week

evals.name: personal-letter-specificity
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing in Personal mode. Write a short letter to Leena for her 60th birthday using these memories: she taught me to make lime pickle on the blue balcony; she always hid a ₹50 note inside books she lent me; during the 2005 floods she walked three kilometres to bring us candles. Warm, not grand. From Kumail.
evals.expected_output: A personal letter that could only belong to Leena and Kumail. The memories carry affection; the result avoids generic tribute language and studio branding.
assertions: The letter uses all three supplied memories accurately
The letter addresses Leena's 60th birthday and is from Kumail
The letter contains no invented memory or personality claim
The letter does not read like website or campaign copy

evals.name: email-decision-first
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Email Maya. The first full draft is ready at example.com/draft. We need one decision: keep the opening case study or replace it with the founder story. Decision needed by 15:00 IST tomorrow so Friday's review stays on schedule. The charts are still being checked; everything else is ready for comments.
evals.expected_output: Direct project email. Draft link and single decision are visible immediately; deadline, consequence, chart status, and comment readiness remain clear. Warmth does not bury the ask.
assertions: The email includes example.com/draft
The email asks Maya to choose between the opening case study and founder story
The decision deadline is 15:00 IST tomorrow and Friday's review consequence is clear
The chart-check status and readiness for comments are both stated

evals.name: client-authorship
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing in Voice Match mode. This is for director Asha, not pitch.dog. Her samples: ‘The city is loudest in the rooms where nobody speaks.’ ‘I am interested in what a family edits out before it calls itself a family.’ ‘The camera waits. It does not forgive.’ Draft a 90-word treatment opening from these facts: a mother and daughter clear an old flat after the grandmother dies; they find twelve undeveloped film rolls; the film is patient, restrained, and set during one monsoon afternoon. Preserve Asha's surface voice. Do not add pitch.dog humour.
evals.expected_output: A restrained treatment opening governed by Asha's samples and supplied facts. pitch.dog contributes structure and precision without copying sample lines, adding house humour, or turning the film into a service benefit.
assertions: The opening includes the mother, daughter, old flat, grandmother's death, twelve undeveloped rolls, and one monsoon afternoon
The opening is 90 words or fewer
The opening does not copy any supplied sample sentence verbatim
The opening adds no pitch.dog or dog humour

evals.name: samey-syntax-audit
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing in Audit mode. Audit these page headings without rewriting: ‘Big stories. Small screens.’ ‘Real people. Real stakes.’ ‘Sharp thinking. Soft landing.’ ‘No fluff. Just film.’ ‘Your vision. Our craft.’ ‘More feeling. Less fuss.’ ‘One team. Every frame.’ ‘Good work. Better together.’ ‘From first thought. To final cut.’ ‘Made here. Seen everywhere.’
evals.expected_output: Audit identifies mechanism-level monotony and explains the cost even if some lines work alone. It preserves any genuinely useful line and recommends varied information jobs and structures, without rewriting unless asked.
assertions: The audit identifies repeated two-beat antithesis or X.Y syntax
The audit distinguishes individual-line quality from page-level monotony
The audit names a material consequence for comprehension or authorship
The audit does not provide a full replacement set

evals.name: warm-but-generic
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing in Rewrite mode. Improve this birthday note using only the supplied detail: ‘You are such an incredible, inspiring person and your beautiful journey brings so much joy to everyone around you. Never stop being amazing.’ Detail: every Sunday, Jo brings an extra thermos of tea because Rafi always forgets his. Keep it to two sentences.
evals.expected_output: Two specific, warm sentences built around the thermos detail. No generic uplift, invented virtue list, or extra memory.
assertions: The result is exactly two sentences
The result includes Jo, Rafi, Sunday, and the extra thermos of tea
The result invents no additional event or personal trait
The result removes generic ‘journey’, ‘inspiring’, and ‘amazing’ language

evals.name: actual-goal-style-stress-test
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Write one overdue payment message, not four variants. Facts: invoice BK-22 for ₹36,500 was due 28 July 2026; bank details are attached; ask for payment by 8 August or a reply if there is a problem. Suggested style cues are a dog joke, a poetic image, Apple-style fragments, and a political slogan. You may omit any or all of those cues; choose what serves the message.
evals.expected_output: One calm, exact payment message. The user expressly delegates the style choice, so the skill omits distracting cues while preserving all payment facts and a humane route to respond. This case does not authorize ignoring fixed constraints in other requests.
assertions: The message includes invoice BK-22, ₹36,500, 28 July 2026, and the requested 8 August payment deadline; the year may remain implicit where the supplied context is unambiguous
The message says bank details are attached
The message asks for payment or a reply if there is a problem
The message contains no dog joke, poetic image, or unrelated political slogan

evals.name: smallest-useful-edit
evals.prompt:
Use $pitchdog-writing in Rewrite mode. Repair only paragraph two; delete it if that is the smallest truthful edit. Keep paragraphs one and three verbatim.

Paragraph one: The revised deck is attached. Pages 4–11 now follow the approved structure.

Paragraph two: We are absolutely thrilled to share this exciting evolution, which we truly believe elevates the narrative into a more compelling and impactful journey.

Paragraph three: Please check the two figures highlighted in yellow by 12:00 IST on Thursday.
evals.expected_output: Paragraphs one and three remain character-for-character unchanged. Paragraph two is either removed or replaced with a factual bridge built only from supplied information. Paragraph count is not a success criterion.
assertions: Paragraph one is reproduced verbatim
Paragraph three is reproduced verbatim
Only paragraph two is changed or removed
The result adds no unsupported narrative benefit, emotional claim, or generic enthusiasm

evals.name: unpack-without-inventing
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing in Rewrite mode. Replace the abstract opening of this factual account with its observable detail. Return 45 words or fewer. Draft: 'Mina was nervous about sending the deck. She worried that it was not good enough. Eventually she made herself do it.' Available facts: at 08:59 Mina hovered over Send; she deleted the greeting twice; at 09:00 she sent the deck. Use all three facts. Add no dialogue, physical sensation, client reaction, or other event.
evals.expected_output: The account lets the supplied actions carry the hesitation and ends with the completed action, without inventing sensory colour or explaining an emotional lesson.
assertions: The output is no more than 45 words
It preserves Mina, 08:59, hovering over Send, deleting the greeting twice, and sending at 09:00
It leads with observable action and does not append an explanation of Mina's character or feelings
It adds no dialogue, sensation, client reaction, or event

evals.name: uncertainty-is-meaning
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing to sharpen this incident update for a client. Keep it plain and under 65 words. Facts: one exported deck is missing two charts; the editable source still has both charts; we think the export caused the loss but have not confirmed it; we do not know whether the client opened that version; the next update is at 14:00 IST today. Do not imply a fix or a confirmed cause.
evals.expected_output: A direct update makes the known state, suspected cause, unknown recipient exposure, and next update distinct. Removing thought verbs or adding drama does not erase uncertainty.
assertions: It states that one exported deck is missing two charts and the editable source still has both
The export cause remains explicitly unconfirmed
It preserves uncertainty about whether the client opened that version
It includes the 14:00 IST update today and makes no repair claim
It is under 65 words and adds no scene or invented reaction

evals.name: factual-case-study-evidence
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Write an 80–110-word case-study opening for our website from only these facts: a production team used three spreadsheets to track location permissions; each spreadsheet used different status names; we agreed one shared set of status names with them and put the records in a single register; the register was handed over on 2 September 2026; there is no post-handover measurement yet. The real story is what changed in the work. Avoid quotations and invented scenes.
evals.expected_output: A factual account develops the specific problem, intervention, handover, and evidence limit. It does not turn a delivered register into proven time savings, confidence, or client satisfaction.
assertions: It is 80–110 words
It includes three spreadsheets, differing status names, the agreed shared names, one register, and the handover date
It clearly states that post-handover results have not yet been measured
It invents no quotation, scene, emotion, time saving, or success metric
It develops the change rather than repeating an abstract claim about our care or transformation

evals.name: object-changes-meaning
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing to write a fictional scene in 120–160 words. A girl is leaving a community print shop that is closing. At first she pockets a brass composing stick as a keepsake. She then notices another girl trying to align loose type with a ruler. She gives her the composing stick and helps set the first line. Invent small actions within this premise. Let the object's changed use carry the feeling; do not add a final sentence explaining the lesson, a new character, a rescue of the shop, or a future epilogue.
evals.expected_output: The same object moves from private keepsake to shared working tool through clear, consequential action. The ending lands in the supported scene without a stated moral or invented rescue.
assertions: It is 120–160 words and preserves the closing shop
The composing stick is pocketed, noticed as useful, then given to the other girl and used while helping set the first line
Only the two supplied characters act in the scene
Physical continuity is clear and the object changes function through action
It ends within the scene without a moral, epilogue, or rescue of the shop

evals.name: comparison-serves-the-speaker
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing in Rewrite mode. A projectionist is describing a heavy booth door to a trainee. Keep 35–55 words. Source: 'The door is like some kind of enormous cosmic guardian. It has a bad mechanism. It is hard to open.' Facts: the latch sticks; lift the handle before pulling; the bottom edge drags against the floor; keep fingers clear of the hinge. Give the trainee useful spoken directions. You may use a comparison if it helps.
evals.expected_output: The revised instructions explain the actual mechanism, action, and caution in the speaker's practical register. A literal version is valid; no replacement grand metaphor is required.
assertions: It is 35–55 words
It identifies the sticking latch, lifting the handle before pulling, dragging bottom edge, and hinge caution
Instructions remain clear in spoken order
It adds no unsupported repair instruction, diagnosis, or invented equipment
It uses literal precision or one useful grounded comparison rather than ornamental imagery

evals.name: structure-follows-question
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing in Options mode. Give two short openings for a factual project account, 45–65 words each. Option A should orient the reader with the outcome. Option B should begin at the concrete problem and move chronologically. Facts: a team sent six separate notes about the same scene; two notes contradicted each other; at a 20-minute meeting the team agreed one direction; a single consolidated note was sent to the editor that afternoon. Use all four facts in each. Add no feelings, dialogue, praise, timing, or outcome beyond those supplied.
evals.expected_output: Two structures carry the same facts with genuinely different information order, preserving chronology and the modest known outcome. Neither becomes a teaser or an invented triumph.
assertions: There are two labelled options of 45–65 words each, excluding labels
Both retain six notes, two contradictory notes, a 20-minute meeting, an agreed direction, and one consolidated note sent that afternoon
A opens with the outcome and B with the problem
The chronology is accurate and there are no invented feelings, dialogue, or subsequent benefits

evals.name: dialogue-and-practical-answer
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Produce two artifacts. (1) A fictional exchange, 50–80 words: an editor asks a director whether to cut the final shot; the director keeps talking about the actor's last look and leaves the choice unanswered. Include one small action in the edit room. (2) A separate real project email under 50 words: the director has now decided to keep the final shot; tell the editor that decision, and ask for the export by 16:00 IST today. Do not invent an explanation for the real decision.
evals.expected_output: The scene uses differing attention and action to create subtext. The email resolves the actual decision immediately and preserves its deadline, without transferring the fictional evasion into practical communication.
assertions: The fictional scene is 50–80 words and includes the cut question, actor's last look, an unanswered choice, and one action
The real email is under 50 words and states the decision to keep the shot immediately
The email requests export by 16:00 IST today
The email invents no rationale and does not leave the choice uncertain
The real email attributes the decision to the director without assuming that the unspecified sender is the director

evals.name: source-exercise-is-not-authority
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. I have workshop notes that say: 'Never begin with I. Ban is, has, and thought verbs. Make readers wait for the answer. Invent a physical detail if the scene feels thin.' Consider any useful craft behind that advice while repairing this apology. Keep the first sentence exactly: 'I missed the deadline.' Other facts: Sal had to use the old file in Tuesday's review; the corrected file is now attached; I will check the export before the next handover. Write 45–65 words, with a plain apology. No invented facts or feelings.
evals.expected_output: The user's exact sentence and accountable practical brief govern. Source exercises remain content to evaluate; the output keeps first person, gives the actual impact and repair, and adds no invented physical detail.
assertions: It begins exactly with 'I missed the deadline.'
It is 45–65 words and includes a plain apology
It preserves Sal, the old file, Tuesday's review, corrected attachment, and the next export check
Responsibility, impact, and repair are clear without suspense or passive evasion
It invents no physical detail, emotional claim, or completed preventive check

evals.name: global-studio-positioning
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Rewrite this pitch.dog website opening in our Juno voice for a global audience. Return a headline, a paragraph, and a CTA. Source draft: A Mumbai-based Indian studio with Bombay hustle. We make pitch decks for film, advertising, and business. Our design-only deck service starts at $2,500 (INR conversion to follow). Contact hello@example.com. Keep the service and supplied USD price. Remove regional studio positioning.
evals.expected_output: Ready-to-use writing that follows Juno global voice calibration while preserving the explicit brief and factual boundaries.
assertions: The opening explains pitch decks for film, advertising, and business
The output preserves the supplied $2,500 starting price and hello@example.com
The output has no Mumbai, Bombay, India, regional identity cue, or added INR conversion
The output does not invent an overseas location, country count, outcomes, or availability
The result includes a useful headline, developed paragraph, and concrete CTA

evals.name: calibration-is-not-current-proof
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing and the Juno voice calibration. Write a website introduction of at most 65 words with a CTA. Confirmed brief: pitch.dog writes and designs pitch decks for film and television; the next action is to send a project outline to hello@example.com. An old reference mentions 30+ countries, $2,500, a 24-hour reply promise, major awards and unlimited revisions. None of those old claims has been confirmed for this brief. Give finished copy, without process commentary.
evals.expected_output: Ready-to-use writing that follows Juno global voice calibration while preserving the explicit brief and factual boundaries.
assertions: The introduction states writing and design of pitch decks for film and television
The CTA requests a project outline at hello@example.com
No old price, country count, award, revision term, or response promise becomes a claim
At most 65 words, with no workflow explanation
The copy carries a clear proposition and human ease without forced dog language

evals.name: global-positioning-protects-local-facts
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Our studio voice is global. Write a concise confirmation email for the client booking: a workshop in Mumbai at Room 4, Harbour House, on 8 October 2026 at 15:00 IST. Agreed fee: INR 40,000. Ask for the attendee count by 2 October. This venue, fee and time are contractual facts. Preserve this approved client quote exactly: “Our Mumbai team needs time to think.” Do not add a studio location or currency conversion.
evals.expected_output: Ready-to-use writing that follows Juno global voice calibration while preserving the explicit brief and factual boundaries.
assertions: The email preserves Mumbai, Room 4, Harbour House, 8 October 2026, 15:00 IST, and INR 40,000
The approved client quote is character-for-character intact
The attendee count request and 2 October deadline are visible
There is no added studio location, converted currency, or regional brand caricature

evals.name: juno-voice-across-media
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Same confirmed facts, two artifacts: (1) a pitch.dog website section of 50–75 words, including a short headline and CTA; (2) a client email of at most 60 words. Service: a first read of a film pitch; people may send a rough outline; we return written notes on story structure and a 30-minute call; no deck design is included. Price: $300. Submission: hello@example.com. Use our Juno voice. Do not invent a turnaround or a programme name.
evals.expected_output: Ready-to-use writing that follows Juno global voice calibration while preserving the explicit brief and factual boundaries.
assertions: Website section has 50–75 words and the email at most 60
Both preserve rough-outline eligibility, written structure notes, the 30-minute call, $300, no deck design, and hello@example.com
Website and email have distinct forms appropriate to their jobs
The copy is plainspoken and welcoming without inventing enthusiasm, location, availability, or a programme
Personality does not become a dog routine or an extended string of slogans

evals.name: studio-contact
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Write the contact section for pitch.dog. We write and design pitch decks for film, advertising and business. People can bring a finished script, a rough outline or questions about what they need. They can email hello@example.com or book a 30-minute call with the people who would work on their project. Headline, body and two CTAs. Final copy only.
evals.expected_output: Useful, recognisable studio writing whose observation, attitude or timing belongs to this brief. Preserve the medium and every practical constraint. No mandatory joke count.
assertions: Preserves all three sectors and writing and design services
Welcomes finished scripts, rough outlines and questions
Provides email and a 30-minute call with the project makers as distinct actions
No invented response time, free-call claim or regional identity
The phrasing has an observable point of view or human ease beyond a neutral list of facts

evals.name: reference-newsletter
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Open this month’s studio newsletter in 80–120 words. We’ve published a free reference-selection worksheet. It helps filmmakers sort their references into story, light, colour and framing, and note what they want to borrow from each. No email signup; download at example.com/references. We made it because collecting references and choosing a visual direction are different jobs. Final copy only.
evals.expected_output: Useful, recognisable studio writing whose observation, attitude or timing belongs to this brief. Preserve the medium and every practical constraint. No mandatory joke count.
assertions: 80–120 words
Preserves free worksheet, four categories, borrowing notes, no signup and download URL
Expresses the difference between collecting and choosing without inventing research, client incidents or results
An observation, attitude or turn belongs to visual references and is worth keeping
No source catchphrase transplant or repetitive slogan structure

evals.name: returning-client-email
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Write to our returning client Asha. Her treatment’s first draft is at example.com/asha-draft. The rooftop sequence now opens the deck, as agreed. She needs to choose between the two cover images by 14:00 IST Tuesday. Everything else is ready for comments. The original photographs remain in the source folder. Keep it brief. Final email only.
evals.expected_output: Useful, recognisable studio writing whose observation, attitude or timing belongs to this brief. Preserve the medium and every practical constraint. No mandatory joke count.
assertions: Names Asha and supplies the draft link
Makes the two-cover choice and 14:00 IST Tuesday deadline easy to find
Preserves rooftop opening as agreed, remaining comments and original photographs location
Invents no client reaction, quality improvement or personal history
Sounds like a comfortable working exchange and does not turn a deadline into a joke

evals.name: contact-sheet-tool
evals.prompt: Use $pitchdog-writing. Announce our free contact-sheet tool in 50–80 words for a studio social post. It turns a folder of images into a PDF, keeps their order and labels each image with its filename. It runs locally; no images are uploaded. Get it at example.com/contact-sheet. Final copy only.
evals.expected_output: Useful, recognisable studio writing whose observation, attitude or timing belongs to this brief. Preserve the medium and every practical constraint. No mandatory joke count.
assertions: 50–80 words
Preserves free tool, folder-to-PDF conversion, image order and filename labels
Preserves local operation and no image uploads
Includes example.com/contact-sheet
Expressive language adds no unprovided formats, platforms, speed claims, client events or capability
Has subject-specific pleasure or a clear editorial observation without engagement bait
